ingredients: Oil: 1 tbsp coconut oil (or neutral oil)
1 tbsp minced fresh turmeric (or 1 tsp ground turmeric)
1/2 tsp Indian red chili powder (or 1 tsp regular chili powder)
Salt, to taste (about 1 tsp kosher salt to start)
1 cup (180–190 g) red lentils (or split red lentils)
1 can full-fat coconut milk (13.5 oz / 400 mL)
For extra creaminess, blend/purée a portion of the curry with an immersion blender.
Spice control: omit chiles for mild; use 1 (seeds removed) for medium; use 2 (seeds in) for spicy.

steps: Rinse lentils in cold water until the water runs clear.
Heat a large deep skillet/saucepan over medium-high heat and add the oil. When shimmering, add garlic, ginger, fresh turmeric (if using), and serrano pepper. Cook ~2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add cumin, coriander, chili powder, curry powder, garam masala, salt, and black pepper. Cook 30–60 seconds until fragrant. (If using ground turmeric instead of fresh, add it here.)
Pour in vegetable broth and scrape up browned bits. Add lentils + crushed tomatoes; stir well.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20–25 minutes until lentils are cooked through and mostly softened. If needed, add a few spoons of broth/water and cook ~5 minutes more.
Uncover and stir in coconut milk + almond butter; adjust salt/pepper. Simmer uncovered 5–8 minutes until thick and creamy.
Stir in lemon juice + cilantro; turn off heat.
Serve with basmati or jasmine rice and Indian flatbread (roti/paratha/naan).
